## 2. Counts per class

| class | count | share |
|---|---:|---:|
| DUP | 62 | 30% |
| FOLD (incl. FOLD+HOOK) | 73 | 35% |
| LOCAL | 55 | 26% |
| STALE | 12 | 6% |
| STATE | 12 | 6% |
| **total** | **208** | |

Of the 73 FOLDs, **8 are FOLD+HOOK** — a recurrence record plus a mechanically
enforceable trigger.

Read differently: **74 of 208 files (36%) restate something a directive or hook
already enforces**, and another 12 actively misdescribe current tooling. Roughly
40% of the store is deletable without losing a fact.

## 4. Contradictions

1. **`Spec H<N>` vs `Test H<N>`.** `feedback_spec_trigger_not_test` records the
   operator's correction that the Lane 3 spec trigger is `Spec H<N>`;
   `3-lane-protocol.md` R-0220 says "HITL says 'Test #N'". Both are load-bearing
   and one is wrong in every session that reads it. Ranked #1 above.
2. **`gha` vs `gh-as`.** `reference_two_account_routing` mandates
   `~/.local/bin/gha`; `universal-agent` R-0014 mandates
   `harmonic-forge/tools/gh/gh-as`. **Both binaries exist on disk.** Two live
   wrappers for one rule is exactly the drift the rule exists to prevent.
   `reference_kenekted_github` compounds it by still prescribing the banned
   `gh auth switch`.
3. **Scheduling link.** `feedback_always_include_scheduling_link` says use
   `calendar.app.google/RukfGog2DNTuKuqU7` **only**, explicitly retiring the
   others. `reference_marc_scheduling_link` (newer, 2026-08-31) says use
   `calendar.app.google/sv4TyYivd6FTdpLi8`, and MEMORY.md's index carries that
   second one. Neither file mentions the other. A drafting session will pick
   whichever it reads first.
4. **Time-of-day framing.** `user_location_timezone`'s "How to apply" tells the
   session to use Pacific time for greetings and time-of-day language.
   `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` § Never reference time-of-day bans the entire category
   with no exceptions, and explicitly says verify-first has already failed.
5. **Detail/evidence section.** `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` § BLUF says the detail
   section "exists precisely so nothing has to be dropped" and that an empty
   section must be declared. `feedback_bluf_discipline_recurring` (4th/5th
   corrections) says default to omitting it entirely. The memory is the newer
   operator instruction.
6. **Other lanes' owed work.** `feedback_dont_track_other_lanes_owed_work` says
   never report what another lane owes; `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` § YOUR NEXT ACTIONS
   says never write "None" when a lane trigger is outstanding, and
   `feedback_your_next_actions_includes_lane_triggers` reinforces it. The
   reconciling distinction — *my* posted artifact's trigger vs. a standing tally
   of someone else's work — is written down nowhere.
7. **Gemini's lane status.** `project_current_lane_tooling` says Gemini was
   eliminated 2026-08-31 as not capable enough. `universal-lane1` § Current lane
   assignment and `3-lane-protocol` R-0193/R-0194 still document Gemini as
   approved for Lane 1, partial for Lane 2, and policy-armed for Lane 3. The
   directive that claims to be authoritative for "what's actually running today"
   is the stale one.
8. **`Estimate` vs `Tier`.** `feedback_warn_on_8pt_issue_trigger` reads the board
   `Estimate` field, deleted in hrse#966, and tells the session to confirm Lane 2
   is on Opus — while `project_fable_vs_opus_model_split` records that Fable
   satisfies `deep` tier since forge#314.
9. **Milestone list.** `reference_hrse_current_milestone` correctly states that
   `CLAUDE.md`'s hardcoded milestone list is stale and a standing-rule violation
   ("if a field can be read from GitHub, it must not appear in the doc").
   Verified live: `CLAUDE.md:190` still reads `Open: 2.7 | 2.8 | 2.9 | 3.0 |
   Later | Platform`, with 2.7 closed. The memory is right and the directive is
   wrong.
10. **Filing order vs. fold-first.** `feedback_file_issue_before_implementing`
    ("file before the first line, always") predates and sits in tension with
    `universal-agent` R-0039–R-0043's fold-first bar and
    `feedback_always_file_dont_ask`'s high bar. The order rule and the threshold
    rule are compatible but have never been stated together.

Five of the ten oversized non-index files are DUP or STALE. The store's bulk is
concentrated in incident logs for rules that have since been promoted into
directives — the promotion happened, the log never got trimmed.

**MEMORY.md index health:** 207 of 208 files are indexed; link targets all
resolve. Findings:

- **One file is not indexed at all:** `feedback_never_close_without_lane3.md` —
  and it is a near-verbatim duplicate of the indexed
  `feedback_never_close_without_lane3_no_exceptions.md`. Two files, one rule, one
  of them invisible to the index.
- **Index hook text that no longer matches the file:**
  - `[Current lane tooling] — Claude/Codex/Gemini any lane; Devin retired` — the
    file says Gemini was **eliminated** 2026-08-31.
  - `[L2 pushes, no PR/merge/close](feedback_lane2_never_pushes_or_prs.md)` — the
    hook text was updated for the 2026-09-05 reversal; the **filename** still
    asserts the retired rule, which is what a filename-only glance will read.
  - `[Warn on 8pt issue trigger] — confirm L2 used Opus` — reads the deleted
    `Estimate` field, and Fable now satisfies `deep`.
  - `[Scheduling link] — calendar.app.google/sv4TyYivd6FTdpLi8` — the index picks
    one side of contradiction #3 without noting the other file disagrees.
  - `[H185 fixture seeds via Cypher](project_185_duplicate_phone_test_seeding.md)` —
    the file's own correction block concludes the seeding was **already**
    documented and automated and that the hook text's premise was wrong.
- **Four broken wikilinks** in file bodies:
  `[[feedback_apq_protocol]]`, `[[feedback_lane1_no_constructed_tests]]`,
  `[[project-hrse2-601-test-token-script]]`, `[[hrse#1303]]` (an issue reference
  written in wikilink syntax).


> **Correction (Lane 1, 2026-09-06):** § 4 states each lane worktree has its own auto-memory store. Verified live against transcripts: HRSE2 `-lane2`/`-lane3`/`/tmp/*-impl` sessions resolve to the shared HRSE2 store (58 transcripts reference it; 13 memory writes from lane sessions). The finding that stands is narrower: forge and infra sessions, and Codex/Gemini lanes, have no store; and topic files are recall-loaded, so a lane session still does not reliably see them.
